transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-26
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~55m
Attendees: Ethan Cole (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Tom Harper (Lakeside - Head of ML), Priya Rao (Lakeside - Platform), Samir Patel (Lakeside - CTO)

Summary: Quick scoping for a 6-week POC to validate Redwood inference for customer-facing assistance queries. Focus on QPS, concurrency, token distributions, and pass/fail bench metrics.

Topics: success criteria, traffic modeling (QPS/concurrency), input/output token distribution, latency SLOs, benchmark plan, timelines

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Ethan: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off. i'm ethan cole from redwood, maya is our SE, we focus on inference perf and workload sizing. tom, want to intro lakeside briefly?
[00:12] Tom: yeah sure, thanks. we run a customer support assistant across mobile and web, roughly 1k daily active users for the assistant right now, moving to 10k in next six months. primary goal is to reduce avg handle time and deflection. we're evaluating Redwood for a POC to validate latency and cost numbers.
[00:30] Maya: great, do you have baseline qps / concurrency today and token stats? even ballparks help.
[00:36] Tom: right now peak qps is small, like 2-3 qps with concurrency about 4-5, but during promo periods we saw bursts up to 15 qps sustained minutes. avg input token length is 80 tokens, but median is closer to 45, output typically 120 tokens. there's a long tail - 95th pct input can hit 400 tokens when customers paste long convo history.
[01:00] Priya: to add, our front-end runs some pre-filtering, so about 30% of requests are short (<=20 tokens) and 10% are long (>250). most are chat-like with multi-turn context, we currently send last 3-5 turns.
[01:18] Maya: mmm okay, that's helpful. for the POC we'll want token distribution histograms and a sample of payloads. also want to confirm success criteria — latency, cost, correctness thresholds?
[01:30] Samir: for success: p99 latency under 800ms for hosted scenario (for 95% of traffic), and p50 under 200ms; throughput should handle sustained 25 qps in a dedicated test; cost target is better than our current OpenAI spend by at least 20% per successful response. quality: stay within current answer accuracy as measured by our eval set.
[01:52] Ethan: good, we're hearing latency SLOs p99 800ms, p50 200ms, sustained 25 qps test, and cost target -20% vs current. we'll scope both hosted and dedicated configs.
[02:05] [02:05] Maya: quick clarifying on metrics: when you say p99 under 800ms is that end-to-end from the front-end or just inference time?
[02:12] Priya: end-to-end, front-end to model response. network adds about 80-120ms on avg.
[02:18] Maya: noted. so for inference we should aim p99 ~650ms to have buffer. also, send us your 95/99 token percentiles; that informs batch sizing and kv-cache memory.
[02:30] Tom: sure. one question — how does Redwood handle multi-turn KV cache? i may have seen notes about kay-vee cache in the docs but the term got butchered on my side.
[02:40] Maya: yes we support kv cache in Dedicated and we can expose options for hosted too. it saves previous key/values on GPU so multi-turn is much faster after warmup. in the POC we'll test cold vs warm cache 95th pct effects.
[02:55] Ethan: for workload modeling, two approaches: 1) synthetic replay from your logs to reproduce real token distributions and arrival patterns; 2) synthetic mixes that stress long-tail (heavy token) and burst qps. we recommend doing both.
[03:10] Tom: replay would be ideal. can you handle timestamp jitter and client-side batching? our logs are in kinesis.
[03:18] Maya: yep we can take a sample export (s3 or shared drive). we have a load harness that can replay inter-arrival times or run closed-loop qps targets. share a 7-day sample at 1% and we can model.
[03:30] Samir: on concurrency, if we do hosted, what's the typical concurrency per model instance? like how many in-flight tokens per GPU.
[03:38] Maya: depends on model size and quantization. for a 7B-ish quantized to int4, we can get high token throughput and high concurrency (dozens of in-flight). for 13B/70B tails, concurrency per instance drops. we'll provide model mapping recommendations.
[03:54] [03:54] Priya: are you planning to run quantized models for the POC? we have security concerns around model variants.
[04:00] Ethan: yes — security remains top. quantization is an execution detail; we can certify that data-in-flight is encrypted, keys via your KMS for private deployment, and we can do Dedicated with customer-managed keys. for hosted we'll provide SOC2 attestation and encryption at rest.
[04:17] Tom: good. another operational question: what about batching? will batching harm latency for short requests?
[04:24] Maya: batching is workload-aware. short requests often get fast-path without waiting; but when you accept slight increase in p50 you can reduce cost by larger batch sizes. for your mix (30% short, 60% medium, 10% long) we typically tune dynamic batching thresholds to avoid harming tail latencies. we'll include cost/latency tradeoff curves in the benchmark deliverable.
[04:45] Ethan: okay let's talk numbers for the POC bench. We propose: week 1 - ingest logs and define dataset; week 2 - replay tests and baseline hosted runs (single region); week 3 - dedicated cluster sizing and model variants; week 4 - extended stress tests (25 qps sustained, bursts to 100 qps); week 5 - security/cost analysis and final report; week 6 - wrap and handoff. does that timeline align?
[05:10] Samir: that's reasonable but we may need to shift security deep-dive earlier. our compliance team needs to review KMS and SSO before any dedicated infra is provisioned.
[05:20] Ethan: sure we'll book a security call week 2 or 3 depending on availability.
[05:24] [05:24] Tom: for the benchmarks, can you capture these metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens per sec, tokens per request, per-token cost estimate, GPU utilization, and failure rates?
[05:35] Maya: yes we'll provide a spreadsheet with columns: request_id, timestamp, input_tokens, output_tokens, latency_ms, model_variant, quantization, region, success_flag. we'll also provide aggregated charts.
[05:48] Priya: how do you estimate per-token cost? our finance folks want a simple calc they can run.
[05:52] Ethan: we publish unit economics: cost per token based on model variant and avg GPU utilization. in the POC we'll provide modeled cost for your observed token mix and then show sensitivity to batch size and cache hit rate. we'll include an example calc so finance can plug numbers.
[06:08] Tom: ok. a couple of tricky things — we have GDPR and data residency concerns; some customers are EU-only. can the dedicated cluster be provisioned in eu-west with customer-managed keys?
[06:18] Maya: yes for Dedicated we can provision region-specific pools and integrate with your KMS/HSM for key management. for Hosted, we have region options but with Redwood-managed keys unless you opt for Private deployment. we'll add that to the security call agenda.
[06:32] [06:32] Priya: about traffic modeling - what arrival model do you use? poisson vs bursty poisson? our traffic has diurnal patterns and occasional campaign spikes; we saw a 10x spike for 3 minutes last quarter.
[06:45] Maya: we support replay of exact timestamps (traffic-preserving) and synthetic models: poisson, peaky bursts, and heavy-tailed inter-arrivals. for the spikes we'll run separate stress tests to validate autoscaling and fallback policies.
[06:58] Ethan: for sizing, we'll produce two recommended configs: 1) conservative dedicated cluster for sustained peak qps (e.g., sustain 25 qps with 95th token percentiles), 2) cost-optimized hosted with fallback to larger model variants for quality-critical paths. we'll show expected GPUs, mem, estimated monthly cost.
[07:18] Tom: what about concurrency at the app layer vs GPU queue? our platform has a gateway that limits concurrency to 200 concurrent user sessions overall, but backend calls per session are async. how do you simulate that?
[07:29] Maya: we can model closed-loop where client waits for response and open-loop where calls are fire-and-forget. we need your gateway behavior to choose the right model. please include a short doc on your gateway limits.
[07:40] Priya: will you run cold-start tests as well? cold KV cache makes a huge difference for multi-turn.
[07:45] Maya: yes cold vs warm cache will be explicit in tests. typically cold cache p99 can be 2-3x warm for long context. we'll measure both.
[07:56] [07:56] Tom: on quality, can we include our evaluation harness? we run an automated rubric against 5k prompts.
[08:02] Ethan: absolutely, include that so we can run model variants against your eval set and compare delta vs baseline. that will be part of pass/fail criteria.
[08:10] Samir: final question - what's the go/no-go criteria after the POC? beyond the perf numbers, we need integration effort under 3 engineer-weeks and a security signoff.
[08:21] Ethan: we'll propose success criteria doc: 1) perf: p99 < 800ms end-to-end for 95% traffic, sustain 25 qps in stress test 2) cost: modeled per-response cost at least 20% lower 3) quality: no regression on eval set (delta < 5% on key metrics) 4) ops: integration work less than 3 engineer-weeks 5) security: signoff on SOC2 + KMS/SAML or Private deployment option
[08:44] Maya: also add fallback behavior documented - if dedicated capacity drops below threshold we failover to hosted or smaller model variant.
[08:51] Priya: that's important.
[08:54] [08:54] Ethan: ok next steps recap: we'll get a list of logs and payload samples from priya, maya will send benchmark config, i will send pricing and pilot scope, and we'll schedule a security deep-dive next week.
[09:07] Tom: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[09:10] Ethan: thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites and links.
